LESSON: WHO IS CREATION

Grade: PP1
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: GOD’S
Topic 1.1: Who is CREATION

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Who is CREATION. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Where does He live?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify God as his/her heavenly • Learners could be guided to recite simple Father. short poems on God as his/her Sole
2. respect God as the Father of Creator, based on respect for mankind, God.(Genesis 1:27)

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WHO IS CREATION
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Who is CREATION helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: WHO IS CREATION
Study Who is CREATION like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify God as his/her heavenly • Learners could be guided to recite simple Father. short poems on God as his/her Sole

What this means
In this part you learn to identify God as his/her heavenly • Learners could be guided to recite simple Father. short poems on God as his/her Sole. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify God as his/her heavenly • Learners could be guided to recite simple Father. short poems on God as his/her Sole.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Who is CREATION” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify God as his/her heavenly • Learners could be guided to recite simple Father. short poems on God as his/her Sole. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Respect God as the Father of Creator, based on respect for mankind, God.(Genesis 1:27)

What this means
In this part you learn to respect God as the Father of Creator, based on respect for mankind, God.(Genesis 1:27). You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respect God as the Father of Creator, based on respect for mankind, God.(Genesis 1:27).
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Who is CREATION in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respect God as the Father of Creator, based on respect for mankind, God.(Genesis 1:27). Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Who is CREATION is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Who is CREATION” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify God as his/her heavenly • Learners could be guided to recite simple Father. short poems on God as his/her Sole)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Who is CREATION in your own words. (skill: respect God as the Father of Creator, based on respect for mankind, God.(Genesis 1:27))

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Who is CREATION to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify God as his/her heavenly • Learners could be guided to recite simple Father. short poems on God as his/her Sole.
3. Practise this skill: respect God as the Father of Creator, based on respect for mankind, God.(Genesis 1:27).
4. Make one local Kenya example of Who is CREATION from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Who is CREATION: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Who is CREATION?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Where does He live?
2. What is your CREATION awareness • Learners are guided in small groups to name?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Who is CREATION means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify God as his/her heavenly • Learners could be guided to recite simple Father. short poems on God as his/her Sole.
5. Be able to: respect God as the Father of Creator, based on respect for mankind, God.(Genesis 1:27).

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
